questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the flagger says otherwise.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal traffic laws as if there is no construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the flagger's directions.
questions.explanation: Be ready to slow down and be careful when a sign, flagger, or police officer tells you to. Not following their directions is against the law and unsafe for construction workers.

questions.question: When approaching a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, drivers should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn before passing on the left side.
Keep driving when you think children have finished getting off.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: When a school bus is stopped with its stop signal showing, you must come to a complete stop. Do not go until the stop arm is pulled back.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should generally:

options.text: Drive faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Highway entrance ramps have acceleration lanes. When merging, turn on your signal, look for an opening in traffic, speed up to match traffic speed, and merge into the opening.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
You must come to a full stop at this intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Stop completely if traffic requires it.

questions.question: A steady yellow light at an intersection means:

options.text: Go.
Let other cars go.
Slow down and get ready to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: Signaling your intentions before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb:

options.text: Is only needed if other traffic is nearby.
Is a good habit and the law requires it.
Is only needed during the move, not before.
Is not needed if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a good habit and the law requires it.
questions.explanation: Signal well before you change lanes or turn. The law requires you to signal for at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle left or right. Always signal when leaving a curb so other drivers know your plans.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, you should:

options.text: Stop right away and let it pass.
Move to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
Drive slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, you must yield to an emergency vehicle using lights and/or a siren from any direction. Move as far right as possible and stop, but not in an intersection.

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to complete a left turn. You should:

options.text: Signal and keep your wheels turned left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so drivers will let you through.
Drive around the back of a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels prevent you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A speed limit is:

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed on a road when conditions are dangerous.
The highest or lowest legal speed on a road when conditions are ideal.
The suggested speed on a road when conditions are ideal.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed on a road when conditions are ideal.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed on a road when conditions are ideal. You can drive slower than the limit, but faster is illegal. Drive slower in school zones, work zones, or bad weather. If conditions make the posted speed unsafe, drive slower.

questions.question: If a vehicle using high beams comes toward you, you should look toward ____ of the road.

options.text: Either side
The center
The right side
The left side

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side
questions.explanation: If an oncoming vehicle has bright high beams on, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see the road well enough to stay on your path until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: In New Jersey, drivers under 21 are considered to be driving under the influence at a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.01 percent.
0.05 percent.
0.1 percent.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 will be penalized if their blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is 0.01 percent or higher.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Lowers blood alcohol concentration.
Stops the effects of alcohol.
Does not change blood alcohol concentration.
Raises blood alcohol concentration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change blood alcohol concentration.
questions.explanation: Coffee does not reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC). While it may help you stay awake, it cannot lower your BAC or make you sober.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Lane closed ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns that a traffic signal is ahead, so be ready to stop for a red or yellow light.

questions.question: Which of the following helps drivers stay in the correct lanes for turning on some highways?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: Arrows on the road show which lanes to use for specific purposes, such as driving straight or turning.

questions.question: After you stop for a school bus that is unloading children:

options.text: Do not move until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
Speed up quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm extended and lights flashing, watch for children walking along the side of the road. Always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: You must be extra careful around a pedestrian using a white cane because:

options.text: They are deaf.
They are a police officer.
They are blind.
They have poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are blind.
questions.explanation: When near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down, yield the right-of-way, and proceed carefully. Be ready to stop to prevent injury.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
Only yield when the pedestrian has the legal right-of-way.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle, regardless of who is at fault. Always yield to all pedestrians, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Check for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: Drivers should be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians because:

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.
They always have the right-of-way.
They don't have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers look but don't see motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians. These are harder to spot because they are smaller, move faster, and have less noticeable lights. Always watch carefully for these smaller road users.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, you should:

options.text: Drive even slower.
Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass.
Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road, if you are driving so slowly that cars are backing up behind you, you must pull over and let them pass. Only drive well under the speed limit when conditions require it.

questions.question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?

options.text: A rectangular red sign.
A circular green sign.
A diamond-shaped yellow sign.
A triangular orange sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign.
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle symbol is an orange triangle that reflects light. Vehicles with this emblem drive 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait for your body to remove the alcohol naturally.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to remove the alcohol naturally.
questions.explanation: Only time lowers your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers do not reduce your BAC or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they cannot change your BAC.

questions.question: Before turning left, what must you do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Let oncoming vehicles go first.
Move to the right side of your lane.
Wait for oncoming traffic to get a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let oncoming vehicles go first.
questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic signal, you must let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.

questions.question: You are waiting in a line at a stop sign. The vehicles ahead pass through with no cross traffic. What must you do?

options.text: You can go through without stopping again.
You must stop again at the stop sign before going.
You can slowly roll past the stop sign.
You can follow the car in front without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop again at the stop sign before going.
questions.explanation: You must always make a complete stop at the stop sign and check for traffic before proceeding. Do not let other cars pressure you to skip your stop.

questions.question: You are stranded in a snowstorm. What should you do?

options.text: Leave the car and go find help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car. You are more likely to be found there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. You are more likely to be found there.
questions.explanation: Stay in your car and wait for help. You are easier to find when you stay in your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm is dangerous.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in suburban residential areas when no other speed is posted?

options.text: 10 mph.
35 mph.
45 mph.
65 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 mph.
questions.explanation: The default speed limit in suburban residential areas is 35 mph. Always follow posted speed limit signs if they show a different speed.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to where you came from.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to where you came from.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to your previous lane.

questions.question: What can happen if your exhaust system leaks?

options.text: Your engine will use too much oil.
Your car will need a tune-up sooner.
You may become drowsy while driving.
Grass fires may start on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may become drowsy while driving.
questions.explanation: A leaky exhaust system releases toxic gases. These fumes can make you drowsy while driving and can be very dangerous. They can cause serious harm or death.

questions.question: What should you do if a traffic light is not working due to a power outage?

options.text: Park your car off the road and wait for the power to come back.
Use hand signals to show other drivers what you plan to do.
Turn on your hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers the same way you would at a four-way stop, then proceed carefully when it is your turn.

questions.question: What must you do when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights?

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Move to the right side and stop.
Stop right where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, move to the right side of the road immediately and stop.
